EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours have been dominated by the funeral of martyred Iranian Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, marked by significant crowds, calls for revenge against the US and Israel, and the appointment of a new IRGC Navy Commander. US President Trump stated that the US "dismantled Iran," granted a week-long pause in negotiations out of "kindness" for the funeral, and confirmed a potential meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu next week. Concurrently, Israeli forces intensified operations in southern Lebanon, killing a Hezbollah operative and conducting widespread strikes, leading Netanyahu to reportedly postpone further actions in one area at Trump's request amidst fears of Iranian retaliation.

IRAN
The funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, referred to as the "martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution" who was "assassinated on the first day of Operation Lion's Roar" in February, entered their second day. State media reported "massive crowds" and "millions" of mourners in Tehran, with calls for revenge against the United States and Israel. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi acknowledged representatives from over 70 countries attending the funeral. Mojtaba Khamenei, the son of the martyred leader, was reportedly blocked by security officials from attending his father's burial in Mashhad on Thursday due to fears of an Israeli assassination attempt or the use of his presence to locate his hideout.

Ali Ozma'i was officially appointed as the Commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy, replacing Ali Reza Tangsiri, who was reportedly killed in the war. Iran's acting defense minister warned of a "firm and decisive response" to any violation of the Iran-US ceasefire agreement, while Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi cautioned against military adventurism by "extra-regional powers" in the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian Intelligence Ministry reported dismantling several "US-Israeli-linked terrorist teams" in southeastern Iran.

Regarding internal politics, four senior Iranian officials and two IRGC members reportedly told the New York Times of deep divisions within the conservative camp, with factions vying for influence over the new Supreme Leader's political future. Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf stated that Iran's resistance has inflicted "political and military defeat" on the US and Israel. President Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized the importance of continuing the martyred leader's path and upholding the flag of resistance.

Economically, Iran's Central Bank denied a New York Times report regarding a letter about food reserve shortages. The National Iranian Oil Refining and Distribution Company affirmed no disruptions in fuel supply. Iran and Serbia agreed to establish a joint working group for technological cooperation, spanning AI, space industry, data transit, fiber optics, data centers, and digital economy.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon escalated following the identification and killing of an armed Hezbollah operative in the Majdal Zoun area. The IDF's 551st Brigade located and neutralized the operative after a chase. Division 679 was reported to have destroyed a neighborhood in Lebanon where one of its soldiers was severely wounded on Thursday. Israeli fighter jets carried out airstrikes targeting Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, and forces detonated residential buildings in the Al-Doura neighborhood of Bint Jbeil. Additional strikes and demolitions were reported in Hadatha, Tebnine, and an airstrike in Mansouri.

Politically, President Trump confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu requested a meeting at the White House, potentially occurring as early as next week after the NATO summit. Trump remarked that he and Netanyahu "get along great" and that Netanyahu "knows who the boss is." Reports indicate that Netanyahu postponed a military operation in the Ali al-Taher area of southern Lebanon at Trump's request, reportedly due to fears of Iranian retaliation. The security cabinet is scheduled to convene tomorrow evening. MK Yuli Edelstein announced his departure from the Likud party after 23 years, stating his intention to form a new political framework for the right, opposing the "Basic Law: Torah Study" which could exempt Haredim from military service. Minister Itamar Ben Gvir canceled a planned trip to New York due to visa issues and fears of protests and potential legal action against him in the US.

The N12 reported 15 murders in the north within a week and 146 murders in Arab society since the start of 2026, marking a 22% increase compared to the same period last year.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF conducted artillery attacks in the southern Gaza Strip.
In the West Bank, Israeli settlers carried out an arson attack on a Palestinian café in the Wadi al-Sha’ar area, south of Nablus. Settlers also set fire to Palestinian farmlands in the town of Turmus Ayya, northeast of Ramallah. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the "completely unacceptable" and "abhorrent" expansion of Israeli settlements and associated violence in the West Bank, stating it directly undermines the prospect of a two-state solution.

LEBANON
An armed Hezbollah operative was killed by Israeli forces in the Majdal Zoun area of southern Lebanon. The IDF reported that the 551st Brigade engaged and eliminated the operative within Israel's buffer zone. Lebanese channel Al-Manar reported that Israeli military helicopters used machine guns to fire at the town of Majdal Zoun. Israeli military operations included Division 679 destroying a neighborhood where an Israeli soldier was previously wounded. Israeli fighter jets conducted airstrikes targeting Bint Jbeil, and Israeli forces detonated residential buildings in the Al-Doura neighborhood of Bint Jbeil, as well as buildings in Hadatha and Tebnine, and an airstrike in Mansouri. Lebanese Al-Akhbar, a Hezbollah-affiliated newspaper, reported that indirect technical talks between Tehran and Washington in Doha failed to resolve "deep disagreements" on several issues, including the "complexities of a ceasefire in Lebanon." Iran's Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi reiterated Iran's firm stance on the necessity of ending Israeli aggression and the complete withdrawal of occupiers from Lebanon. Enemy assessments cited by Naya indicate approximately 1,200 armed operatives south of the Litani River. A Kuwaiti court sentenced a Kuwaiti citizen to 10 years in prison for alleged links to Hezbollah.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, security tensions were reported in the city of Salamiya in the eastern Hama countryside, attributed to Jabhat al-Nusra gangs kidnapping several Alawite citizens. Qatar's Minister of Foreign Affairs affirmed support for Syria's unity, sovereignty, independence, and reconstruction efforts.
In Iraq, Muthanna, Maysan, and Wasit provinces declared Wednesday, July 16, a public holiday, with Maysan and Wasit extending the holiday to Thursday, July 17, to allow citizens to participate in the funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iraqi tribes and clans formally requested that the funeral of the martyred leader be held on Iraqi soil. The Popular Mobilization Forces (Hashd al-Shaabi) in the Middle Euphrates command are coordinating with security forces and relevant authorities for the funeral arrangements. Iraqi F-16 airstrikes targeted terrorist dens in the Dibs district of Kirkuk. Unidentified aerial bombardment was reported near the Bardia border in Kirkuk, targeting suspected ISIS strongholds. An ISIS operative identified as Ahmed Hussein Ali Hussein al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Maria, was killed during clashes with Iraqi security forces in Kirkuk. ISIS also reportedly kidnapped a citizen in the Altun Kupri area of Kirkuk. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced plans to address the armed factions and security files with Turkey, including "the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and Sinjar." The Iraqi Ministry of Justice reported recovering over $25 million in looted Iraqi funds in the past two years, while Iraqi security forces arrested a drug dealer in Baghdad with 14,000 Captagon pills.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's national airline denied foreign media reports of selling five Boeing 777-200 aircraft to a sanctioned Iranian company, stating the planes were sold to a different, non-Saudi entity in June 2023. Ansar Allah's Mohammed al-Farah criticized Saudi Arabia's "insistence on suffering losses," asserting that its decisions are not its own and that it squanders funds on "insignificant figures" in Yemen and Lebanon. Qatar's Foreign Minister expressed support for the unity, sovereignty, independence, and reconstruction of Syria. A Kuwaiti court sentenced a Kuwaiti citizen to 10 years in prison for alleged ties to Hezbollah. The Basra Human Rights Commission appealed for intervention regarding Iraqi women stranded in Kuwait after their citizenship was revoked.

Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Iran was reported to have entirely closed the US-supported corridor for passage, leading to US tactical aircraft (one E-3B, six KC-135R, two KC-46A) flying over the Persian Gulf. Turkey's President Erdogan referenced the "Islamabad Agreement" between Washington and Tehran, stating he supports steps to de-escalate regional tensions and monitors efforts to disrupt the agreement.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  The funeral ceremonies for martyred Iranian Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei were held in Tehran, drawing large crowds and international delegations, with calls for revenge against the US and Israel.
2.  US President Donald Trump stated that the US "dismantled Iran," asserting that Iranians are "begging for a deal," and that the US provided a "week break" in negotiations for the funeral.
3.  The next round of indirect negotiations between the US and Iran is scheduled for July 11 in Pakistan, focusing on sanctions, frozen assets, and the nuclear file.
4.  Ali Ozma'i was appointed as the new Commander of the IRGC Navy, replacing Ali Reza Tangsiri, who was reportedly killed in the war.
5.  Israeli forces killed an armed Hezbollah operative in the Majdal Zoun area of southern Lebanon and conducted widespread strikes, including destroying a neighborhood and detonating residential buildings in Bint Jbeil.
6.  Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly postponed a military operation in the Ali al-Taher area of southern Lebanon at the request of US President Trump, citing fears of Iranian retaliation.
7.  Iran was reported to have closed the US-supported corridor for passage through the Strait of Hormuz, prompting the flight of US tactical aircraft over the Persian Gulf.
8.  Deep divisions within Iran's conservative camp over the new Supreme Leader's future were reported, with Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly blocked from his father's burial due to assassination fears.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high, particularly between Iran and Israel. Iranian calls for "revenge" and former IRGC Commander Yahya Rahim Safavi's assertion of an "existential war" with Israel signal continued intent for confrontation. US President Trump's statements, including the claim that the US "could take out all the officials at the funeral with one shot," while presented as a rhetorical point, underscore the volatile nature of the US-Iran relationship. Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon and the reported postponement of an operation due to Iranian retaliation fears highlight a direct flashpoint. The alleged closure of the US-supported Strait of Hormuz corridor by Iran, followed by US tactical aircraft flights, poses a significant risk to regional maritime security and could escalate quickly. Active flashpoints include southern Lebanon, the Strait of Hormuz, and southeastern Iran, where "US-Israeli-linked terrorist teams" were reportedly dismantled. The Israeli assessment of a potential breach of the Gaza agreement by Hamas within 2-3 months suggests a risk of renewed fighting in Gaza by September. US deployment of 8 A-10 Warthog aircraft to Jordan indicates a potential increase in military posture in the broader region. Red lines include Iran's acting defense minister's warning of a "decisive response" to any MoU violation and the Deputy Foreign Minister's warning against military adventurism in the Strait of Hormuz.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** saw President Trump make strong statements regarding Iran, claiming they are "begging for a deal" and that the US granted a "week break" for Khamenei's funeral out of "kindness." Trump also confirmed a potential meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu next week. US military posture in the region includes the deployment of 8 A-10 Warthog aircraft to Al-Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan and the flight of a US E-3B early warning aircraft, six KC-135R refuelers, and two KC-46A refuelers over the Persian Gulf after Iran reportedly closed the US-supported Strait of Hormuz corridor.

**Gulf States** like Qatar reiterated support for Syria's unity, sovereignty, and reconstruction. Saudi Arabia denied selling Boeing 777-200 aircraft to a sanctioned Iranian company. A Kuwaiti court sentenced a citizen to 10 years for alleged links to Hezbollah.

Among **EU members**, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the "completely unacceptable" expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank and the "abhorrent" violence associated with it, stating it undermines the two-state solution.

**Russia's** Deputy Security Council Chairman Dmitry Medvedev attended Khamenei's funeral, remarking that the Strait of Hormuz is a strategic asset for Iran comparable to nuclear weapons. Russian President Putin and US President Trump conversed for over an hour, with Putin providing an assessment of the war in Ukraine and Trump offering to assist with a settlement ahead of the NATO summit in Turkey. Russia also claimed to have seized five settlements in eastern Ukraine.

**China's** representative at the funeral affirmed commitment to strengthening relations with Iran and expressed hope for a US-Iran ceasefire.

**Turkey's** President Erdogan warned against the current Israeli government "spreading the smell of gunpowder and blood" in the region again and emphasized that any solution must originate from regional countries. He also mentioned closely monitoring efforts to disrupt the "Islamabad agreement" between Washington and Tehran.

**Pakistan's** Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the "wisdom, visionary leadership, and profound influence" of Ayatollah Khamenei, stating that Pakistan stands in solidarity with Iran. Pakistan is set to host the next round of US-Iran negotiations.

**Yemen's** Ansar Allah movement sent a delegation to Khamenei's funeral, with one of its political bureau members criticizing Saudi Arabia for its persistent losses and misallocation of funds.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions emerged regarding the attendance at Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral. While Iranian state media and officials claimed "millions" and "massive crowds" filled Tehran's Grand Mosalla, opposition channels (Mamlekate, Omid Dana) and Al Arabiya estimated the crowd size to be much smaller, between 200,000 to 300,000, and even less than previous public events or former President Rafsanjani's funeral. Some opposition sources suggested "shock and awe of regime leaders from non-participation of people."

Unverified claims include Omid Dana's assertion that Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi signed an agreement with Oman concerning the division of the Strait of Hormuz corridor, which would limit Iran's control. There is also no independent verification of the exact details or nature of the "Islamabad agreement" mentioned by President Erdogan.

Propaganda indicators are evident in both Iranian and US narratives. Iranian state media consistently framed Khamenei as a "martyred leader" and emphasized national unity, the broad international presence at the funeral, and calls for revenge, portraying a strong, unified front. US President Trump's statements, such as "we dismantled Iran," "they're begging for a deal," and "we gave them a week break because we are nice," appear to be highly theatrical and intended to project strength and magnanimity. Opposition reports frequently used pejorative terms for Iranian officials and alleged "artificial crying" or the use of AI to inflate funeral imagery.

Reporting gaps include the lack of specific details regarding the "US-Israeli-linked terrorist teams" dismantled in southeastern Iran, such as their affiliations, targets, or the extent of US-Israeli involvement. The precise terms, duration, and conditions of the "week break" in negotiations mentioned by Trump are also not fully detailed, nor is the extent of any prior US-Iran "ceasefire agreement" or "MoU" mentioned by Iran's acting defense minister.
